Pittsboro.wildlife_intro:
Pittsboro pairs a historic core with fast growth, and its calls pair up too: bats and raccoons in the courthouse-town housing, groundhogs and snakes on the farm edges, and new-community animals arriving with each cleared tract.

The Haw River corridor keeps raccoons, opossums, and beavers' workings along the bottoms, while the big new developments northeast inherit pond snakes and attic squirrels from the woods they replaced.

The Piedmont year runs in waves through Pittsboro. Cold months drive squirrels and rodents into attics, spring opens raccoon denning in chimneys and crawlspaces, and summer brings bat maternity colonies — protected statewide, with eviction by a licensed Wildlife Control Agent limited to August 1 through April 30. Autumn sends a second squirrel and rodent push for winter rooms. Our crew starts with a full roofline, attic, and crawlspace inspection, then removes the animals and seals every entry we find, because closing only the obvious hole rarely holds.

In Goldston the calendar is written by litters and weather.
